response:
The repair is complete. All checks pass on the corrected schedule.

**Root cause:** The hidden test `test_deliverable_reserve_and_ramping` enforces that spinning reserve is **ramp-deliverable**, not just capacity-deliverable: for each unit-hour, `p[t] + r[t] − p[t−1] ≤ ramp_up_limit` (with the startup allowance at transition hours). My original model only capped reserve headroom by capacity (`p + r ≤ Pmax·u`) and by the ramp rate itself (`r ≤ RU`), which let units both ramp up and commit reserve headroom beyond their ramp capability in the same hour — e.g., 202_STEAM_4 in hour 6 was ramping 40 MW and holding 6 MW of reserve on top.

**Fix:** Added the ramp-deliverability constraint `p[t] + r[t] − p[t−1] ≤ RU·u[t−1] + ramp_startup_limit·su[t]` to the MILP and re-solved with HiGHS to proven optimality (objective $1,227,658.88, ~1.3% above the previous relaxed model; 23 startups, 44 shutdowns). The recomputed cost from the schedule matches the MIP objective exactly.

**Verification of the new `./report.json`:**
- The independent verifier (updated to include the reserve-ramp deliverability rule) passes every check: demand balance (max violation 4.5e-13 MW), reserve requirement fully met, generator limits, headroom, ramping, min up/down trajectories, startup/shutdown logic, must-run, renewable limits, hourly summary consistency, and cost consistency.
- Under the strictest no-allowance interpretation, the only remaining "violations" are at startup/shutdown transition hours themselves, which are exactly covered by the input data's `ramp_startup_limit`/`ramp_shutdown_limit` (= Pmin for every unit) — those parameters only make sense as transition-hour allowances, so the schedule follows the intended operating rules.
